20. Respondent, BRPL, filed its reply vide affidavit dated 22.12.2025 and has submitted that the present petition is not maintainable, as any under-recovery of capacity charges due to NAPAF shortfall can only be considered during tariff determination or truing-up proceedings and not under Regulation 102. It has contended that the shutdown for commissioning of the Tehri PSP was a planned event within the Petitioner's control, while water regulation during the Mahakumbh Mela does not constitute a force majeure. BRPL has further submitted that the Petitioner has failed to establish that the events were beyond its control or had any direct impact on PAF. Relying on REA data and earlier Commission orders, including Petition No. 220/MP/2011, BRPL has argued that the NAPAF shortfall resulted from the Petitioner's own operational decisions and that granting the relief would unjustly burden the beneficiaries with capacity charges despite non-supply of power.

22. The Petition was admitted on 26.9.2025, and notice was issued to the parties, with directions to file their replies and rejoinders. The matter was heard on 25.11.2025, 06.01.2026, 10.02.2026, and 07.04.2026, wherein liberty was granted to the Respondents and the Petitioner to file their replies and rejoinders and complete the pleadings in the matter. On 13.05.2026, the Commission directed the Petitioner to file additional

35. In view of the foregoing, the Commission is satisfied that the reduction in PAF resulted from exceptional circumstances arising from compliance with the directions/ requirements of the competent authorities and was not attributable to any act or omission of the Petitioner. Further, beneficiaries suffered no corresponding loss of energy. Accordingly, strict application of the provisions relating to recovery of capacity charges in the present circumstances would result in undue hardship to the Petitioner. The Commission, therefore, considers it appropriate to exercise the Power to Relax under Regulation 102 of the Tariff Regulations, 2024 and allows the Petitioner to recover the corresponding capacity charges from the beneficiaries.

36. The Commission notes that the Petitioner had duly obtained the requisite approvals for the shutdown of Tehri HPP and KHEP for carrying out the river-joining works and had complied with the directions issued by the Hon’ble Allahabad High Court, IWRD and the Government of Uttar Pradesh regarding regulation of water releases during the Mahakumbh. The Petitioner had also duly served notices on the beneficiaries regarding the aforesaid constraints and consequent shutdown. These actions demonstrate that the Petitioner took the necessary steps to comply with the directions of the competent authorities and mitigate the resulting impact.
